text:
Jamie Oleksiak, the "Big Rig," is one of the unluckier defensemen in the league this season. The Canucks have scored seven fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and our numbers flag him as due. He scored against Anaheim last week, with Daniel Wagner noting the Ducks left him alone at the top of the zone because "he's Jamie Oleksiak."

On a bad team, he has been one of the better defensive options. Vancouver is about six points of expected goal share better with him on the ice than off it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why: he stops 18% of the entries aimed at him, well above the typical 11%. The weak spot is moving the puck out, with only 26% of his exits keeping possession.

He's not an offensive defenseman, and his 16.7% shooting will settle. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season in Seattle coming almost entirely from defense. Our range has him at 17 to 30 points over a full season. At 33 he's a steady third-pair presence, and the kind a contender might want for the spring.
headline: Oleksiak, steadier than the results
